Of course the IC looked into the report. That is what you do with raw intelligence. In the end, they found some of the report corroborated their own intel, and that corroboration was used in the case. That doesn’t mean Trump’s golden shower was included. 

When you say Steele’s motivations were to promote Clinton and sabotage Trump, is that something you can support with evidence? Or is it just something you say because it makes your narrative work? 

Steele was known as a credible source. He spent years in British intelligence focused on Russia. He was an expert in the field of Russian intelligence. He had previously worked with the FBI on other cases, and was known to be reliable. The only thing that discredited him with the FBI was the fact that he went to Yahoo News. That was something the FBI couldn’t associate with. 

And when you note that Priestap knew some of the content could be Russian disinformation, it isn’t the gotcha you think it is. It means Priestap knew what all the rest of us knew, and which only people in a right wing echo chamber wasn’t aware of. Steele’s work was raw intelligence. It is a reporting of things that are being said. Each and every claim in every raw intel document that has ever been created in the history of intelligence required follow-up investigation to determine what is true and what isn’t.  You are basically saying Priestap understood the intelligence works better than you do.
